newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian logging a threat to economy - Bank.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian logging a threat to economy - Bank.

text.p: Illegal logging in Cambodia in violation of bans on cutting and the export of timber was depriving the government of revenue and threatening economic reform, the Asian Development Bank (ADB) chief said on Thursday.
ADB president Mitsuo Sato, in Phnom Penh to inaugurate the bank's resident mission in Cambodia, said illegal logging continued to be a worry among Cambodia's aid donors.
"Widespread illegal logging and export out of Cambodia are major concerns of the aid community and have undermined major economic reform efforts here," Sato told a news conference.
"Funds derived from logging should be reflected in the state budget and a framework for sustainable forestry management should be developed by the government," he said.

The World Bank said in a report on Cambodia's forestry policy last year that the industry was capable of generating half of annual government revenues but had provided only an estimated 12 percent of total government income in 1995.
Last year the International Monetary Fund cancelled a $20 million loan installment over concerns about excessive logging and the loss of potential government revenue.
Sato said the ADB was providing the government with funds for a major forestry review this year.

Cambodia has tried on several occasions to impose bans on the felling of trees and the export of timber. The latest log export ban came into effect at the beginning of the year but environmentalists say significant illegal logging continues.
Sato said the ADB had proposed a loan portfolio worth a total of $385 million for Cambodia for the 1997 to 2000 period.
The lending programme would focus on five sectors - infrastructure, agriculture and water resources, finance and industry, the social sector and the environment, he said.
Sato said the ADB would also provide Cambodia with technical assistance to help it prepare for full membership of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN), due later this year.
